messages:
eva: Heads-up: ran a long chat workload with prefix caching + eviction + compaction. Observed fused-attn kernel assertion when KV pages had small gaps after compaction. Repro steps + log below.

matt: repro steps?

eva: 1) enable prefix cache, 2) simulate churned prefixes to trigger eviction, 3) compactor runs async -> kernel crashes during next request. Log:
```
[ERR] kernel/fused_attn.cpp: assert(kv_layout.contiguous) failed at 0x7f8bb...
stack: fused_attn_run -> kernel_dispatch -> serve_loop
KV page map: [0x1000 len=4096][0x2000 len=2048][free 512][0x3000 len=1024] -> non-contiguous physical layout
```

kevin: Looks like the fused path assumes block-aligned, contiguous KV blocks for fast vector loads. Small holes from compaction/eviction metadata cause the assert.

sophia: Options off the top of my head: 
1) make kernel tolerant (scatter-gather iovec) so it can gather non-contiguous pages.
2) make compactor produce physically contiguous buffers (memcpy compaction).
3) keep an indirection layer the kernel can consult (pointer table) so kernel still sees a logical contiguous view.

matt: Tradeoffs: (1) increases kernel complexity and may lose perf for fused path, (2) memcpy is simple but costs CPU and PCIe copies, (3) indirection adds per-token pointer chase overhead and may complicate vectorization.

eva: We need numbers. Also consider DMA pages / pinned memory costs when copying to GPU. I'll put together microbench harness to compare gather vs memcpy on A100 + MI250.

kevin: Quick sketch for kernel fallback: 
```
if (kv_has_holes()) {
  build_iovec_from_pages();          // gather SG entries
  if (num_fragments <= SG_THRESHOLD)
    run_gather_kernel(iovec);       // gather directly inside kernel path
  else {
    memcpy_compact_to_scratch();   // copy contiguous buffer then run fast_vector_kernel
  }
}
```
Estimate: on A100, expect ~10% throughput drop for gather when fragments>8, and ~20-30% cost for memcpy per GB moved depending on PCIe/NVLink config (rough). Need microbench.

sophia: Another lever: adjust compaction policy TTLs and pin hot prefixes so they avoid churn. If we pin a small set of hot KV frames, fragmentation incidence drops. But pinning increases memory footprint.

matt: Can also add a runtime config flag: "kernel_compat_compaction_mode" which uses compaction that prefers physical contiguity when enabled. That avoids kernel changes for customers who want max perf.

eva: Test plan suggestions: fuzz generator to create fragmentation patterns (many small frees, varied hole sizes), run both fused and non-fused kernels, capture latency/throughput, and measure memcpy bytes and gather calls. Add end-to-end load sim with real prefix distributions.

sophia: Metrics to add to Console: kv_fragment_count, avg_fragment_size, compaction_run_time, memcpy_bytes, kernel_gather_calls, kernel_memcpy_fallbacks. Alerts on sustained fragment_count > 500 or avg_fragment_size < 1024.

matt: Also add a small regression test in CI that simulates compaction during ongoing requests and checks fused-kernel path doesn't assert. Mark it slow/opt-in.

kevin: Implementation plan: prototyping order -> 1) harness + microbench, 2) gather-path in kernel prototype (SG gather), 3) memcpy fallback and tuning, 4) compaction-mode toggle + metrics + RFC.

eva: I'll draft the RFC and include perf targets and test matrix. @kevin can you sketch a rough perf delta table for the RFC?

kevin: will do. Rough numbers to include: fragments 1-4 negligible, 5-8 small regression, >16 large regression for gather path; memcpy cost scales linearly with moved bytes. Will quantify after microbench.

devops-bot: ticket created: INF-2048 "paged-kv compaction vs fused-kernel compatibility" assigned to eva

eva: ok I'll add notes to RFC draft and create the fuzz harness issue. Leaving action items: eva -> RFC + harness, kevin -> kernel sketch + perf table, sophia -> dashboard metrics & alerts, matt -> CI test. Thanks everyone. :wave:
